findings.description: The inline policy grants wildcard actions (ec2:*, s3:*, lambda:*, cloudwatch:*) on all resources ('*'), violating least privilege and allowing this IAM user to perform virtually unrestricted actions across multiple services.

A long-lived IAM access key/secret is created for a user with excessive permissions, increasing the risk and blast radius if the credential is leaked; static keys are inherently harder to rotate and audit than temporary role-based credentials.

Creating a standalone IAM user with directly attached permissions (rather than using roles/temporary credentials) combined with an overly permissive policy increases the risk of credential compromise leading to broad account access.
